description: Regression guard for a confirmed miss: an audit kept a deterministic elapsed-time logo sequence in useLoop even though the browser could own its transform/opacity keyframes.
expectedBehavior: Runs the bundled scanner and treats phase-loop-browser-keyframes as a candidate that needs source inspection, not proof

Notices that every visible value is a deterministic function of frame.elapsed and expressible as browser-animatable keyframes, with no live input, physics, layout reads, canvas, or required per-frame side effects
Recommends CSS keyframes or WAAPI for playback instead of useLoop; prefers WAAPI when the runtime-generated multi-target timeline needs imperative control
Requires first-paint CSS to match keyframe zero so WAAPI does not snap after hydration
Keeps phase as the lifecycle layer via useLifecycle so visibility changes call play/pause without rebuilding keyframes, while reduced motion skips setup and renders a meaningful static state
Does not claim WAAPI is always off-main-thread; limits compositor expectations to suitable transform/opacity animation and asks for trace verification
Flags the SVG transform-list write independently of timeline ownership and recommends moving compositor-friendly transform/opacity animation to an HTML wrapper when possible
